messages.subject: RStan memory leak?
parts:
[moved to stan-dev from stan-users]

recover_memory() needs to be called after any evaluations
involving var objects. You can see an example in
log_prob_propto() in:

src/stan/model/util.hpp

You an also just call log_prob in the model with double
values, but that call doesn't drop all the constant terms,
so it gives you a different answer than log_prob_propto
as defined in util.

- Bob

On 10/13/13 5:21 PM, Jared Murray wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> I'm running into a memory issue: Calling log_prob from R is leaking memory for me on multiple platforms with multiple
> models (example follows with 8 schools; after a short while it starts eating RAM .04GB at a time in this case, but I'm
> running out of memory altogether with fewer calls to larger models). Calling grad_log_prob is fine though.
>
> schools_code <- '
> data {
> int<lower=0> J; // number of schools
> real y[J]; // estimated treatment effects
> real<lower=0> sigma[J]; // s.e. of effect estimates
> }
> parameters {
> real mu;
> real<lower=0> tau;
> real eta[J];
> }
> transformed parameters {
> real theta[J];
> for (j in 1:J)
> theta[j] <- mu + tau * eta[j];
> }
> model {
> eta ~ normal(0, 1);
> y ~ normal(theta, sigma);
> }
> '
> set.seed(2)
> schools_dat <- list(J = 8,
> y = c(28, 8, -3, 7, -1, 1, 18, 12),
> sigma = c(15, 10, 16, 11, 9, 11, 10, 18))
>
> fit <- stan(model_code = schools_code, data = schools_dat,
> iter = 1000, chains = 4)
> # this leaks memory
> for(s in 1:1000000) tt=log_prob(fit, rep(0,10))
>
> # but this doesn't
> for(s in 1:1000000) tt=grad_log_prob(fit, rep(0,10))
>
> --

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan memory leak?
parts:
This seems to be an 1.3.0 issue.  After the refactoring, rstan follows 
https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Model-Concept, and only calls 
the log_prob_propto function defined in util.hpp using doubles. 

So this memory issue should not exist in coming version. 

--
Jiqiang
On Sun, Oct 13, 2013 at 8:15 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

[moved to stan-dev from stan-users]

recover_memory() needs to be called after any evaluations
involving var objects.  You can see an example in
log_prob_propto() in:

  src/stan/model/util.hpp

You an also just call log_prob in the model with double
values, but that call doesn't drop all the constant terms,
so it gives you a different answer than log_prob_propto
as defined in util.

- Bob

On 10/13/13 5:21 PM, Jared Murray wrote:

Hi all,

I'm running into a memory issue: Calling log_prob from R is leaking memory for me on multiple platforms with multiple
models (example follows with 8 schools; after a short while it starts eating RAM .04GB at a time in this case, but I'm
running out of memory altogether with fewer calls to larger models). Calling grad_log_prob is fine though.

schools_code <- '
   data {
     int<lower=0> J; // number of schools
real y[J]; // estimated treatment effects
real<lower=0> sigma[J]; // s.e. of effect estimates
}
parameters {
real mu;
real<lower=0> tau;
real eta[J];
}
transformed parameters {
real theta[J];
for (j in 1:J)
theta[j] <- mu + tau * eta[j];
}
model {
eta ~ normal(0, 1);
y ~ normal(theta, sigma);
}
'
set.seed(2)
schools_dat <- list(J = 8,
                     y = c(28,  8, -3,  7, -1,  1, 18, 12),
                     sigma = c(15, 10, 16, 11,  9, 11, 10, 18))

fit <- stan(model_code = schools_code, data = schools_dat,
             iter = 1000, chains = 4)
# this leaks memory
for(s in 1:1000000) tt=log_prob(fit, rep(0,10))

# but this doesn't
for(s in 1:1000000) tt=grad_log_prob(fit, rep(0,10))

--
